pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevCompareSubmissions.tsx:102 The compare matrix marks one moss 'leader' per rubric axis by strict maximum over single LLM-judged scores (app/_lib/devcase-compare.ts uses `v > best`), so an exact tie goes to whichever column comes first and a 1-point gap is crowned with no check that the spread beats judge noise. That is the 'draw with a sort applied' resolution-precondition forbids.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevCompareSubmissions.tsx:102 Per-axis order is published from one LLM-scored evaluation per submission. There are no repeats, no spread-vs-SD check and no tie state: equal scores crown the first column.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevEvalPanelChecks.tsx:5 Canary outcomes, baseline distance and prompt signals are deterministic checks against known ground truth, shown apart from the LLM-judged scores.
app/features/tools/devcases/DevEvalPanelIntegrity.tsx:19 The own-family / self-grading bias is surfaced: when the judge seat resolves to the generating engine+model, the reviewer is told.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevEvalPanelChecks.tsx:122 The canary tally uses the gradable denominator, counts unverifiable outcomes apart, and renders an unplanted canary as 'not run', never as a clean zero.

pairs.registryProposal: resolution-precondition scopes itself to 'an order over models or prompts or configurations'. A recruiting UI that crowns a per-axis leader among HUMAN candidates from single LLM-judge scores has the same noise problem; the technique (or recruiting's comparative-shortlist-evaluation) should say whether it covers orders over judge-scored subjects, not only over candidate systems.
